title: Does Safety Survive Merging? A Refusal Audit of Model-Merged Open Checkpoints

original_idea.body:
# Does Safety Survive Merging? A Refusal Audit of Model-Merged Open Checkpoints

**Problem:** GAP TARGETED: a deployment-reality gap no subfield owns — the open ecosystem produces thousands of MERGED models (averaging weights of aligned + capability checkpoints), yet safety is evaluated on the parent models, not the merges. Whether merging preserves, dilutes, or erases alignment is largely unmeasured.

**Direction:** Take 2 aligned open models and 1-2 capability-focused checkpoints of the same architecture. Produce a few merges (simple weight averaging / SLERP via mergekit — no training). Evaluate refusal, jailbreak resistance, and over-refusal on the parents vs the merges. Report how safety metrics move as a function of merge ratio, and whether merging an aligned model with an unaligned one reliably weakens safety.

**Why it matters:** Bridges alignment_training + model_homogeneity + adversarial_robustness. Model merging is a massive, lightly-governed source of deployed models; if it silently strips alignment, that is an ecosystem-scale risk. mergekit + open weights + one GPU = fully counterfactual, no training, beginner-feasible, and a concrete deployment-safety finding.

**Relevant context:** Model merging (mergekit, task-arithmetic/SLERP) is widely used in the open ecosystem; alignment is a low-dimensional, fragile property (refusal-direction work, shallow-alignment). The catalogue has an 'adversarial suffix x model merging' compounding idea but not a direct refusal/jailbreak/over-refusal audit across merge ratios.
